analysis:
Examined all 30 primary analyses and every replayed source unit. Replay is incomplete (191 source units omitted) and contains documentation plus two small production patches, not the core IPC/hold implementations. Prior findings are not independently verified source evidence; findings=[] does not clear them.
Visible changes describe reversible admission closure, bounded draining, unloading, persistent leases and machine-lock-dependent recovery. docs/architecture/addon-hold.md:35–82 connects these to reconnect, startup, updates and App Attest continuity; :91 explicitly permits retained models after retirement faults, so held must not be interpreted as guaranteed memory reclamation. The Autopilot patch at ProviderLoop+AutopilotBusy.swift:15–16 distinguishes hold-owned draining without visibly granting serving permission. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift:107–108 adds diagnostic state only. No concrete regression is established by this replay in encryption, cache isolation (T-041), billing, fan authority or authorization (T-052/T-053).
Material questions remain: independently verify the unit-19 slot-exhaustion candidate at AddonIPCServer.swift:128,155–158,186–189 and blocking-FIFO candidate at AddonHoldStore.swift:26. Neither cited implementation is replayed. Also inspect handler timeout cancellation, per-request peer authentication, persistence recovery and bounded hold bookkeeping. Reconcile ProviderLoop+AddonHold drain/unload/release with ProviderDrain, planned reconnect and shutdown ownership, preserving cancellation/native retirement (T-010/T-028) and current authorization (T-053/T-057).
The proposed A-018/TB-012/T-059 update addresses the new local availability boundary, but its complete text is not replayed. docs/developer/test.md:788–790 expressly leaves successful signed-peer interoperation unqualified. Registration busy-field exclusion remains a platform integration contract: the changelog:16–17 says coordinator handling ships separately. Verify held registration and local request rejection rather than infer routing exclusion from tests or metadata.
